label: run98a warm committed
definition: Run 98a: MEASURED PROBE, not a keeper - warm-boiler exemption alone on the run-97a keeper base (--coal-warm-committed; bins shares unchanged). Mechanism finding behind run 97b: COAL bins carry $100/MW startup and ONLY the _committed tranche has min-run params, so the P1 startup amortization lands solely on the committed band, pricing it ABOVE the econ ramp top (Parish 2024 committed cleared only at LMP >= ~$20 vs econ from ~$13) - the run-97b 'backfire' was capacity moving into the startup-bearing band, NOT the commitment screen (P2 was off). The exemption: a coal bin with a must-run floor never goes dark (Parish: 8760 CAMPD op-hours every year), so committed dispatch is a hot-unit ramp. Measures: per-plant committed-band response across ALL coal (Parish/Spruce/Martin Lake/Limestone/Oak Grove), 2024 coal split recovery, 2023 split + guard cost, LMP. MEASURED - REJECTED as keeper (the decisive split experiment): 2024 fixed, 2023 detonated. 2024: coal split -8.5 -> -2.2% PASSES, PRB 2024 -0.3% (Parish +3.8 TWh recovered) - proving the startup-markup inversion IS the 2024 coal deficit's mechanism. 2023: PRB +8.8% FAIL, coal split +7.8% FAIL, gas -3.1% FAIL, guards blown (ML 1603 / LS 1215 GWh); committed coal also steals ST_GAS 2024 (-2.98) and CT 2024 (-3.02), lignite 2024 re-flips (-1.14) -> 5 fails. The exempted committed band (~$16) clears in BOTH years - no year asymmetry. VERDICT: fleet-wide warm exemption is a dead lever; the 2024 split is pinned to loss-making self-commitment the energy-only merit order cannot produce without importing the measured behavior (monthly CAMPD p10 floors sized at only +2.15 TWh net in 2024 -> split ~-4.8%, still failing).
